topics.title: Strange News & Oddities
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts discuss bizarre personal experiences like building a ballroom and attempting to influence mattress choices, alongside unsettling accounts of violence including setting a woman on fire after a pageant loss. They also cover tax fraud by HUD appointees, a teenager murdering his father over Miss Teen USA, attempted suicide with a wristwatch, and unusual carvings in the host’s head.

topics.title: Radio Host Argument Over a Mental Patient
topics.summary: A chaotic radio segment devolves into an argument between hosts and a guest (identified as Cher) over Becky, a mental patient. The conversation quickly spirals with insults about appearances, accusations of infidelity, bizarre comparisons to other figures like Andrea Martin and Rob Cameletti, and demands for the guest to remove her clothing.

topics.title: Howard Discusses Movie Spots and Family Dynamics
topics.summary: During the broadcast, Howard discusses his attempts to secure movie spots based on perceived attractiveness, referencing an encounter with Rob Cammelletti and a conversation about family dynamics including jealousy towards others’ privileged lifestyles. He also explores themes of wealth disparity through anecdotes involving a wealthy friend's daughter.

topics.title: Yacht Dreams and War Stories
topics.summary: During a conversation about Howard’s humor and broadcasting experiences after military service, a guest describes an exclusive club offering a 75-foot yacht for members with amenities like tennis courts. The discussion shifts to the origins of family wealth and potential financial backgrounds, including inquiries about guests' fathers' histories.

topics.title: Real Estate Disputes and Family Dynamics
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, the host discusses his wife’s father's wealth stemming from a successful business. They debate college affordability, explore real estate investments with a focus on free listings, introduce a gay comedy troupe, and discuss personal relationships including film projects and phone calls with an acquaintance named dice.

topics.title: Gay Comedy Troupe Discusses Vegas and Personal Lives
topics.summary: A gay comedy troupe recounts their experiences performing in Las Vegas with Wayne Newton, sharing anecdotes about awkward encounters, personal crushes (including Billy Mumey), and the challenges of being comedic performers. They discuss early realizations of sexuality referencing childhood obsessions like Honey West and explore themes of identity within the entertainment industry.
